title: What If the Oceans Got 150 Percent More Acidic?

scenes.text: What if the ocean got 150 percent more acidic? Under high emissions, that is the projection for 2100.
It has already begun. Since the Industrial Revolution, surface ocean pH has fallen by 0.1, about 30 percent more acidic.
The tiniest victims come first. Floating sea snails called pteropods would see their shells dissolve in about 45 days.
Oysters, mussels and abalone struggle to build shells. West Coast oyster hatcheries have already lost larvae in low-pH water.
Reef-building corals would find it harder to grow skeletons, and about a million species depend on coral reefs.
From a boat, the ocean would look the same. The change would be in the chemistry, starting with the smallest shells.
